title: Pseudo-superconducting-diode effect in ferroelectric Josephson junctions
authors: Yaozu Tang, Nienke ten Haaf, Artem Bondarenko, Mazhar N. Ali, Yaroslav M. Blanter
abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE), characterized by unequal critical supercurrents in opposite current directions, enables supercurrent rectification. We propose a magnetic-field-free pseudo-superconducting-diode effect in ferroelectric Josephson junctions with broken inversion symmetry. Using a coupled dynamical model that combines a polarization-dependent RCSJ description with Landau-Khalatnikov-Tani ferroelectric dynamics, we show that ferroelectric polarization switching induces asymmetric critical and retrapping currents under current sweeps. The resulting nonreciprocity is highly tunable via ferroelectric parameters and the sweep protocol and remains robust at finite temperatures. Our work identifies ferroelectric Josephson junctions as a promising platform for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal superconducting devices.
summary: This work proposes that ferroelectric Josephson junctions can exhibit a magnetic-field-free supercurrent diode effect due to the coupling between superconducting currents and ferroelectric polarization switching. By modeling this coupled system using dynamical equations, the authors demonstrate that current sweeps induce history-dependent nonreciprocity in critical and retrapping currents. This identifies FE-JJs as tunable platforms for next-generation nonreciprocal superconducting electronics.
main_problem: The study investigates a magnetic-field-free pseudo-superconducting-diode effect (SDE) in ferroelectric Josephson junctions, which enables supercurrent rectification.
main_result: The nonreciprocity is generated by the history-dependent process of current-induced ferroelectric polarization switching, and this effect persists even at finite temperatures.
method: The authors employ a coupled dynamical model solving for both the Josephson junction dynamics (RCSJ) and the Landau-Khalatnikov-Tani ferroelectric dynamics using numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The system is an inversion-asymmetric Ferroelectric Josephson Junction (FE-JJ). The physics is modeled by coupling a polarization-dependent RCSJ description to the LKT ferroelectric dynamics, governed by coupled differential equations derived from a Lagrangian approach.
key_observables: Asymmetric critical and retrapping supercurrents ($i_c$ vs $i_r$), time-averaged voltage ($V$) and polarization ($P$), and diode efficiency ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Ferroelectric parameters (e.g., spontaneous polarization $	heta_{P0}$), junction damping, temperature ($T$), and the current sweep protocol.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on coupled differential equations derived from a Lagrangian formalism; some discussions neglect voltage-shift terms for simplicity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate hysteresis loops (V vs I) showing asymmetry in retrapping currents, time evolution of polarization and phase during switching, and IV scatter plots confirming thermal effects and resistive states at finite T.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical model via coupled dynamics, analyzes the non-equilibrium nature of the SDE using current sweeps (I-V/I-P traces), explores resonance features, and finally examines the robustness and temperature dependence of the diode effect.
why_interesting: The coupling between superconducting phase dynamics and classical ferroelectric polarization switching provides a rich platform for studying non-equilibrium phenomena in condensed matter systems, relevant to understanding energy dissipation and memory effects in quantum devices.

Potential landscapes are constructed using the time- averaged data and correspond, from left to right, to sweep points I, I’, II, and III in Fig. 2(d). Gray regions/curves indi- cate oscillation amplitudes. (a)–(d) Ferroelectric double-well potential profiles (orange curves) and polarization values (or- ange balls). (e)–(h) Corresponding Josephson-junction wash- board potentials (green curves) and phase values (green balls).

FIG. 4. Histograms of critical (i± c ) and retrapping (i± r ) currents. The temperature T is set to (a) 0.1 K, (b) 0.2 K, (c) 0.5 K, and (d) 1 K. Each histogram (shown on a log- arithmic scale) is constructed from 1000 full current sweeps. The arrows at the top indicate the zero-temperature values of the critical and retrapping currents for reference. The critical temperature of the superconductor is estimated to be Tc ≃0.5 K using simple BCS approximation.
